humanities_role_explanation: M3Exam is a general-intelligence benchmark built from school exams across subjects (language, math, social science, natural science). Humanities-adjacent items (history, language, social studies) are only part of the pool and serve as generic exam questions; the competence tested is general multilingual/multimodal ability, not disciplinary humanities competence.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text multiple-choice questions in 9 languages; about 23% (2,816) require one or more images, marked with placeholders and supplied as image files.
analytical_tasks_explanation: All items are multiple-choice exam questions (accuracy). They mix factual knowledge (history, social science), language questions (e.g. Swahili idiom, Javanese script to Latin transliteration), math/science reasoning, and image-based questions needing cross-image reasoning. Culture-specific knowledge is acknowledged, but no interpretive or genesis-oriented tasks.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Broad multi-subject, multilingual, multilevel exam benchmark for general intelligence.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-4, ChatGPT, Claude-instant, BLOOM, Vicuna; multimodal: BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, Fromage, OpenFlamingo (plus Flan-T5).

published_after_march_2023.note: NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks track; references include May 2023 works.

summary: M3Exam is a benchmark of 12,317 real official exam multiple-choice questions in 9 languages from primary, middle and high school graduation exams, with about 23% requiring images. It evaluates text-only and multimodal LLMs, finding that GPT-4 is the only model above 60% and that low-resource and non-Latin-script languages and complex multimodal questions remain hard.
key_findings: GPT-4 averages 72.92% accuracy (ChatGPT 57.57%, Claude 51.80%); performance is weakest on Javanese, Thai and Swahili. Multimodal models score below 50% overall (BLIP-2 49.06%) and barely beat text-only Flan-T5 (48.30%). Performance does not decrease monotonically with educational level. ChatGPT is weakest in math. English translation helps Thai and Javanese greatly.
facets_explanation: Questions and official answers were collected from real national or regional graduation exam papers by native-speaker collectors; annotators then fixed OCR errors, formatted items and entered the answer from the official answer sets. Questions require external subject and culture-specific knowledge, and data were sourced natively per country rather than translated to retain cultural background. Each item has one correct option.
results_explanation: GPT-4 reaches 72.92 average accuracy in Table 2 (zero-shot). ChatGPT on Thai improves from 34.09 (Monolingual) to 46.49 (EN-Translation) and on Javanese from 37.47 to 50.94 (the latter is the 13.47 gap, rounded up to 14). The paper reports the number of test items only as a total of 12,317, with 3 development questions per subject/level/language held out, so evaluation_set_size is not given as a single figure. No human baseline number is reported (only a passing score line).

humanities_role.quote: we group the questions for each language into four subject categories, namely language, math, social science, and natural science

dataset_size.quote: In total, M3Exam comprises 12,317 questions in 9 diverse languages

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: We primarily evaluate various LLMs in zero-shot settings.

gold_source.quote: collect official exam papers along with their answers at the end of each educational level

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: many questions are closely tied to each specific language, translated data may lose essential information in such cases

answer_multiplicity.quote: As all the questions are multiple-choice questions, we utilize accuracy as the evaluation metric.

reported_format_gap_kind.quote: employing a translate-test approach (i.e., translating target language data to English)

reported_cultural_asymmetry.quote: existing models generally perform worse for non-Latin languages, such as Chinese (despite being relatively high-resource), as well as low-resource languages like Javanese
